questions.text: What does the rollout tool actually do, and who or what moves billing_mode from one state to the next? Is each move a person running a command, or automatic once a gate is met?
In shadow, which engine's result is the one customers are actually charged on, and where does the new engine's output go?
questions.about: shadow and both run both engines / shadow store

questions.text: In both, which engine's charges are real? What does having both engines running mean for the customer's bill?
questions.about: shadow and both run both engines

questions.text: What does the nightly comparison job compare, and what does it write to comparison_results? What counts as a pass for the 7-day and 14-day gates?
questions.about: Gates: shadow to both after 7 days of comparison

questions.text: What does the billing monitor watch, and what condition makes it trigger a rollback by itself?
questions.about: Rollback is manual or via the monitor

questions.text: Walk me through the rollback steps: what does pause_charging stop, what does catch_up catch up on and from where (usage event log?), and what does reconcile fix?
Which rollback steps are skipped and when? For example, what is skipped when rolling back from shadow?
questions.about: Rollback steps are skipped where not needed

questions.text: What is the rollback record, when is it written, and how does a retried step use it to know where it stopped?
What happens if a rollback step fails or hangs, for example while charging is paused? Does charging stay paused?
What exactly resets after a rollback: the day counters, comparison_results, or the Finance sign-off? And what is the 35-day clock counted from?
questions.about: Gates reset after a rollback / decommissioned after 35 days

answers.text: Each forward move is a person setting billing_mode, as the brief requires. The rollout controller is not written yet, so the tool's exact behaviour is not fixed. My decision: the controller refuses a forward move unless its gate has passed, and it never moves on its own. Rollback can be started by hand or automatically by the monitor. The file now says this in the forward-moves section.
In shadow, customers are charged on the old engine's result, which is written to the ledger. The new engine's invoices go only to the shadow store. It never charges and never writes the ledger.

In both, only the new engine's charges are real. It charges through the payment provider and writes the ledger. The old engine still computes every invoice, but into the shadow store, without charging. So the customer's bill comes from the new engine alone, and the old engine's output is only for comparison and standby.

The nightly job compares each customer's old and new invoice totals for each billing period. A mismatch is a difference of more than one cent. It writes one comparison_results row per customer per billing period, holding both totals and a mismatch flag. A night passes when its mismatch rate is under 0.1%. The brief does not say whether the 5,000-invoice minimum counts across the 7 days or each day, so that part is an open question.

The monitor watches the new engine's charge failure rate, in both and new_only only. It starts a rollback by itself when that rate is above 2% over any 10-minute window. Errors in shadow are recorded and never trigger one. The brief does not define the rate's denominator, so that is an open question.

pause_charging stops the new engine's charges. switch_to_old sets billing_mode to old_only. catch_up makes the old engine process the usage events it skipped, read from the usage event log, which keeps 35 days. reconcile goes by customer and billing period: it keeps charges already in the ledger and charges what is due and not yet charged, exactly once. The reason is the brief's rules against charging twice and against dropping a due charge.

From shadow, the new engine never charged or wrote the ledger, and the old engine is already current. So only switch_to_old runs. From both, catch_up is skipped because the old engine kept computing. pause_charging and reconcile still run, because the new engine has charged. From new_only, every step runs. The file now lists the skips in the steps section.

The rollback record is one row, written when a rollback starts. It lists each step and whether it is done. A step marks itself done when it finishes. A retry reads the record, skips the done steps, and runs the rest. Each step must be safe to run twice, so reconcile checks the ledger before charging. I chose this because the brief forbids double charges.

Charging stays paused. A failed or hung step leaves the record showing where it stopped, on-call is alerted, and the step is retried. No later step runs, and the old engine does not start charging until reconcile has finished. The brief does not say how long a pause may last, so that is an open question.

The 7-day count and the Finance sign-off reset, because both are gates and the brief resets gates after any rollback. comparison_results rows are kept as history and do not count toward a gate. The 35-day clock starts when the rollout enters new_only, because that is when the old engine stops and its skipped usage events begin to age out of the 35-day log.

questions.text: How does the new engine get its usage events in shadow and both? Do both engines read the same usage events, or does each have its own copy?
In reconcile, who works out what is due for each customer and billing period? Is it the old engine's invoice, or the new engine's? How does it tell what is already charged?
Who or what does the retrying when a rollback step fails: an automatic loop or a person? How often, and how does the system tell a step is hung rather than slow?
questions.about: Steps are retryable / A rollback step fails or hangs

questions.text: What does the monitor do when a rollback is already running, or when a second trigger fires during one? Can two rollbacks run at once?
What makes a mismatch resolved, and who resolves it? Where is that recorded, given that comparison_results only holds a mismatch flag?
questions.about: both to new_only: no unresolved mismatches

questions.text: Who decommissions the old engine on or after day 35, and what is the gate? What does a manual rollback do after day 35, since there is no way back?

answers.text: Both engines read the same usage event log. The brief says the new engine reads the same usage events, and today the old engine reads that log, so there is no second copy. The file now says so in the modes section.

Due is the old engine's invoice in the shadow store. After rollback the old engine is the billing engine, and it has been computing every invoice in both, and catch_up fills the gap in new_only. Charged is the sum of the customer's ledger rows for the period, because the ledger is the system of record. Reconcile charges only the difference, checking the ledger before each charge. Open: a charge sent but not yet in the ledger, and a ledger total above the due amount, are listed under open questions.

The rollback runner retries automatically, not a person. The brief forbids dropping a due charge, so a stalled rollback cannot wait for someone to notice it. On-call is alerted at the first failure and takes over when retries run out. A step past its time limit without marking itself done is hung. A step still inside the limit is slow. The retry count and time limit are not in the brief, so they are left to the controller design and listed as an open question.

No, two rollbacks cannot run at once. Two runs of reconcile could charge the same customer twice, which the brief forbids. A second trigger, by hand or automatic, is logged and starts nothing. This one-at-a-time rule is the only extra rule added, and the brief requires it.

The nightly job resolves a mismatch. It recomputes every night. A mismatch is resolved when the newest comparison_results row for that customer and period has no mismatch flag, so the state is recorded in comparison_results itself with no new column. A person finds the cause of a mismatch that persists. I did not add a separate resolution record, because the brief fixes comparison_results as totals plus a flag. Whether a person must sign off a resolved mismatch is not in the brief.

A person decommissions the old engine, after 35 days in new_only with no rollback. Decommissioning cannot be undone, and the brief gives a person every forward move, so an irreversible step also goes to a person. From day 35 on, a rollback request is refused and on-call is told. What happens if the new engine fails after day 35 is not in the brief, so it is an open question.

teachbacks.text:
1. Starting point. The system is in one of four modes, held in the flag billing_mode in the config service. Today it is old_only. The old billing workers read usage events, compute invoices, write them to the ledger (the system of record) and charge customers through the payment provider. The new engine is off.

2. Forward move 1, old_only to shadow. A person sets billing_mode to shadow. There is no gate. The controller never moves on its own. From now on the old engine still charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage event log (kept 35 days) and computes its invoices into the shadow store. It never charges and never writes the ledger. The shadow store is a separate store for invoices that are never charged. Errors from the new engine in shadow are only recorded and never start a rollback.

3. The nightly job. Each night it compares each customer's two invoice totals for each billing period. It writes one comparison_results row per customer per period, holding both totals and a mismatch flag. A mismatch means the totals differ by more than one cent. Mismatch rate is mismatches divided by invoices compared. Each night counts as one day. Which two totals are compared is only implied. In shadow they are presumably the old engine's and the new engine's, but the document does not say where each is read from.

4. Forward move 2, shadow to both. A person sets billing_mode to both, but the controller refuses unless the gate has passed. The gate is 7 consecutive days with a mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared. How the 5,000 is counted is an open question. In both, the new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing invoices into the shadow store without charging, so it stays current.

5. Resolving mismatches. A mismatch is resolved when the customer's newest comparison_results row for that period has no mismatch flag. A person finds the cause, and the next night that matches clears the flag.

6. Forward move 3, both to new_only. A person sets billing_mode to new_only. The controller requires 14 days in both with no unresolved mismatches, plus Finance sign-off. In new_only the new engine does everything and the old engine stops. The old engine's skipped usage events then begin to age out of the 35-day log. The day-35 clock starts here.

7. Decommissioning. A person decommissions the old engine once the rollout has been in new_only for 35 days with no rollback. From day 35 on, there is no way back.

8. Rollback triggers. There are two. By hand, on-call can start one at any time up to the day-35 limit. Automatically, in both or new_only, a rollback starts when the new engine's charge failure rate is above 2% over any 10-minute window. Only one rollback runs at a time, and a second trigger is logged and starts nothing. A rollback requested on day 35 or later in new_only is refused and on-call is told.

9. Rollback record. When a rollback starts, a rollback record is written. It holds the steps for the starting mode, all marked not done. For shadow the steps are switch_to_old. For both they are pause_charging, switch_to_old, reconcile, resume_charging. For new_only they are pause_charging, switch_to_old, catch_up, reconcile, resume_charging. The state diagram's rolling_back box also lists catch_up for all modes, which conflicts with the table. I follow the table.

10. Rollback steps run in order.
- pause_charging stops the new engine's charges.
- switch_to_old sets billing_mode to old_only.
- catch_up (new_only only): the old engine processes the usage events it skipped, read from the usage event log, and writes the resulting invoices to the shadow store.
- reconcile: for each customer and period, the amount due is the old engine's invoice in the shadow store, and the amount charged is the sum of that customer's ledger charges. Reconcile charges only the difference, once. It checks the ledger before each charge, so a rerun cannot charge twice.
- resume_charging: the old engine charges again, and only after reconcile has finished.
Each step marks itself done in the rollback record when it finishes. Each step is safe to run twice.

11. Failure during a rollback. If a step fails or hangs, charging stays paused, the record shows the step, and on-call is alerted at the first failure. The runner retries automatically, skipping done steps and running the rest, and no later step runs until the failed one succeeds. A step past its time limit counts as hung. A step still inside its limit is slow, not hung. If retries run out, on-call takes over and charging stays paused. The document does not say what on-call does.

12. After rollback. billing_mode is old_only. To go forward again, a person sets shadow with no gate. The gates start over. The 7-day count restarts at zero, Finance sign-off must be given again, and old comparison_results rows stay as history and do not count. The rollback record is left as history, but the document does not say what ends it.
gaps: How the 5,000-invoice minimum is counted (across the 7 days or per day) is not stated, so I cannot say exactly when the shadow-to-both gate passes.
The denominator of the 2% charge failure rate is not defined, so I cannot say precisely what triggers the automatic rollback.
The document does not say how many automatic retries run or what time limit makes a step hung, so I cannot say when retries run out.
It does not say how long charging can stay paused before a person must act, or what on-call does once they take over after retries run out.
It does not say how reconcile treats a charge that has reached the payment provider but is not yet in the ledger, so reconcile's difference calculation is incomplete for that case.
It does not say what reconcile does when the ledger holds more than the old engine's invoice, because there is no refund rule.
It does not say what happens if the new engine fails after day 35, when rollback is refused.
The diagram lists catch_up for every rollback, but the table says only new_only runs it. I assumed the table is right, and the document does not say which governs.

It does not say which two totals the nightly job compares in each mode, or where it reads each from. It does not say how the controller learns that a gate has passed or whether the person checks it. It does not say how the 14-day both count or the 35-day clock is recorded.

It does not say whether the new engine in both or new_only can fail in ways other than charge failures that matter, or how the new engine learns charging is paused. It does not say what happens to customers' charges during the pause, and it does not say how the 2% window is measured over time.

The fresh junior could not tell which governs. Fixed: the diagram now draws each starting mode's steps, matching the table.; The nightly comparison does not say which two invoice totals it compares or where each is read from, so the junior could not explain the step that feeds the shadow-to-both gate. teachbacks.text:
1. Starting point. The rollout begins in `old_only`. The old billing workers read usage events from the usage event log, compute invoices, write them to the ledger (the system of record) and charge customers through the payment provider. The new engine is off. The current mode is stored in `billing_mode`, a flag in the config service.

2. Moving to `shadow`. A person sets `billing_mode` to `shadow`. This move has no gate. The controller never moves on its own. Now the old engine still charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage event log and computes its invoices into the shadow store. It never charges and never writes the ledger. If the new engine errors in `shadow`, the error is recorded only and no rollback starts.

3. The nightly comparison. Each night, a nightly job compares the two engines' invoice totals for each customer and billing period, "wherever each engine writes its invoice". It writes one `comparison_results` row per customer per period. The row holds both totals and a mismatch flag. A mismatch means the totals differ by more than one cent. The mismatch rate is mismatches divided by invoices compared. Each night counts as one day.

4. Gate for `shadow` to `both`. The controller refuses the move unless there have been 7 consecutive days with a mismatch rate under 0.1%, and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person then sets `billing_mode` to `both`. If the gate has not passed, the controller refuses.

5. Running in `both`. The new engine now charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing its invoices into the shadow store, without charging, so it stays current. The nightly job keeps writing comparison rows.

6. Resolving mismatches. A mismatch counts as resolved when the customer's newest `comparison_results` row for that period has no mismatch flag. A person finds the cause. The next night that matches clears the flag.

7. Gate for `both` to `new_only`. The rollout needs 14 days in `both` with no unresolved mismatches, plus Finance sign-off. A person then sets `billing_mode` to `new_only`. In `new_only` the new engine does everything and the old engine stops. The 35-day clock starts here. The old engine's skipped usage events begin to age out of the 35-day usage event log.

8. Decommissioning. After 35 days in `new_only` with no rollback, a person decommissions the old engine. From day 35 on there is no way back.

9. What starts a rollback. There are two triggers. By hand, on-call can start one at any time, up to the day-35 limit, from `shadow`, `both` or `new_only`. Automatically, in `both` or `new_only`, one starts when the new engine's charge failure rate is above 2% over any 10-minute window. Only one rollback runs at a time. A second trigger is logged and starts nothing. A manual request in `new_only` on day 35 or later is refused, and on-call is told.

10. Rollback record. When a rollback starts, a rollback record (one row per rollback) is written. It lists the steps for the starting mode, all marked not done. `shadow` runs switch_to_old. `both` runs pause_charging, switch_to_old, reconcile, resume_charging. `new_only` runs pause_charging, switch_to_old, catch_up, reconcile, resume_charging.

11. The steps, in order:
 - pause_charging stops the new engine's charges.
 - switch_to_old sets `billing_mode` to `old_only`.
 - catch_up (`new_only` only): the old engine processes the usage events it skipped, read from the usage event log, and writes the resulting invoices to the shadow store.
 - reconcile: for each customer and period, the amount due is the old engine's invoice in the shadow store, and the amount charged is the sum of that customer's ledger charges. It charges only the difference, once, and checks the ledger before each charge so a rerun cannot double-charge.
 - resume_charging: the old engine charges again. It starts only after reconcile has finished.

12. Step bookkeeping. Each step marks itself done in the rollback record when it finishes. A retry skips the done steps and runs the rest. Every step is safe to run twice.

13. Failures during a rollback. If a step fails or hangs (hung means it passed its time limit without finishing; a step still within its limit is only slow), charging stays paused and the record shows the step. On-call is alerted at the first failure. The runner retries the step automatically, and no later step runs until it succeeds. If retries run out, on-call takes over and charging stays paused.

14. End of a rollback. `billing_mode` is `old_only`. To go forward again, a person sets `shadow` with no gate. The gates start over: the 7-day count restarts at zero and Finance must sign off again. Old `comparison_results` rows stay as history but do not count.
gaps: In `shadow` the old engine's invoices are not written to the shadow store, so I cannot say where the nightly job reads the old engine's total from. The document lists this itself as an open question.
The document does not say how the 5,000-invoice minimum is counted, across the 7 days or for each day, so I cannot say exactly when the shadow to both gate passes.
The document does not give the denominator of the 2% charge failure rate, so I cannot say exactly when an automatic rollback fires.
The document does not give the number of automatic retries or the time limit that makes a step hung, so I cannot say when retries run out and on-call takes over.
The document does not say how long charging can stay paused before a person must act.
The document does not say how reconcile treats a charge that has reached the payment provider but is not yet in the ledger.
The document does not say what reconcile does when the ledger holds more than the old engine's invoice. There is no refund rule.
The document does not say what happens if the new engine fails after day 35, when there is no way back.
The document does not say how the controller counts 'days in both' or '7 consecutive days' when a night's job fails or a day has no comparison rows.
The document does not say how Finance sign-off is recorded or checked, or who decides that the gate has passed.
The document does not say how the rollback runner is started or where it runs, or how the 'one rollback at a time' check is enforced.
The document does not say what a 'decommissioned' state does beyond stopping the old engine, or what the person does to carry it out.
